documents.snippet: These guidelines provide new and updated recommendations on the use of point-of-care testing in children under 18 months of age and point-of-care tests to monitor treatment in people living with HIV; the treatment monitoring algorithm; and timing of antiretroviral therapy (ART) among people living with HIV who are being treated for tuberculosis.

documents.title: HIV and Children | NIH - HIVinfo
documents.snippet: Key Points HIV can be passed on to children during pregnancy, at childbirth, or while breastfeeding. This is called perinatal transmission. In the United States, perinatal transmission is very rare, but it is the most common way children aged under 13 years get HIV.
